newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cenbank plans no forex policy change-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cenbank plans no forex policy change-paper.

text.p: A top Brazilian Central Bank official dismissed speculation the bank will alter its foreign exchange policy to stem a growing trade gap, despite market nervousness, a local newspaper said.

"The market is not going to prompt any change whatsoever. Whoever wants to bet is preparing to take the risk of losing that bet," bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco Franco told Gazeta Mercantil in an interview.
Modifying the exchange rate to improve the trade balance is an idea linked to failed past policies, he said. He also dismissed the idea of indexing the exchange rate to inflation.
Franco, one of the author's of Brazil's anti-inflation Real Plan, also said concerns about the trade gap, which grew to a whopping $1.308 billion in October, are exaggerated.
"Regarding the trade balance, there is no number there that scares or reveals the need to alter anything important in the stabilization plan," he was quoted as saying.
"What is relevant and deserves consideration is the behavior of exports. There we have a localized problem."
Asked about worries regarding Brazil's fiscal deficit, slow growth rate and exchange rate, Franco said: "In my opinion, there is nothing that needs to be changed right now."
